Hi all,

Thanks for sending — I reviewed the customer redlines in ACME_OrderForm_Redlines.pdf and pulled the legal-commercial items into a single redline (attached: redlines_legal_track.docx). High-level notes:

1) Minimum commit schedule
- Customer's staged 12-month step-down is reasonable commercially but we should preserve a minimum annual commitment in the MSA Order Form to protect unit economics. Proposed compromise: a 12-month initial term with a stepped minimum (Year 1 = 100% commit, Year 2 = 75% commit, Year 3 = 50% commit) with a mutual termination right for material breach.

2) Pricing appendix
- Fixing list pricing for 12 months is generally acceptable, but we need an explicit carve for pass-through cloud cost spikes (e.g., >20% provisioning cost increase). Suggest: indexing clause tied to observable public cloud pricing indices or specific GPU price index.

3) Net terms & invoicing
- We can accept Net45 for this account if Finance signs off (Marissa). Request: invoices routed to procurements@acmecorp.com with a mandatory PO number field — otherwise invoices will be rejected/delayed.

4) Tax/residency/VAT
- Acme must provide VAT registration evidence and a completed W-8/W-9 equivalent for tax residency. If Redwood is the supplier (US entity), Redwood will invoice without VAT for US-supplied services; for EU supplies, we need to assess reverse-charge applicability. I have requested ACME's VAT certificate.

Action items I propose now:
- Marissa (Finance) to confirm Net45 + PO workflow and whether staggered invoices (quarterly advance + monthly overage) are acceptable operationally.
- Karthik (Sales Ops) to validate SKU/tier stability requirement and whether we can build a 12-month price freeze into the Order Form's annex.
- Jasmine to propose a revised Order Form with tracked comments and a clean v3 for signature.

Posting my tracked redline (attached). If ACME's legal agrees with the stepped minimum and the pass-through carve, we should be able to close with moderate concessions.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

Date: 2028-07-05T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: ACME - initial Order Form draft & redlines attached

Thanks — quick finance perspective:

- Net45: We can accept Net45 for strategic customers, but it changes cashflow and may affect discounts. For approval, I need a signed SOW/order form showing expected ARR. We should document whether any early-pay discounts apply.

- Invoicing cadence: Customer request for a centralized AP mailbox is fine. Strong preference is for one consolidated invoice per billing period with clear PO references. If they want a staggered invoice schedule (quarterly advances + monthly overages), we will need to map revenue recognition and ensure Sales Ops can produce those invoices automatically. That is doable but has operational overhead.

- Taxes: we'll accept Redwood default for supplier VAT responsibility where Redwood invoices from Redwood US entities. For EU supplies or when ACME has a VAT presence, we'll accept reverse-charge if they provide evidence. Please ask ACME to send the tax_certificate_acme.pdf (VAT cert) and the AP remit instructions.

Operational asks for the Order Form v3:
1) Add a mandatory PO number field on the invoice template.
2) Define billing schedule in Annex A (sample language: quarterly advance invoicing + monthly true-up) and include examples for the first 6 months.
3) Add a clause that any change to pricing tiers requires 30 days' written notice except pass-through indexing.

If Sales is comfortable with the stepped minimum proposed by Kimberly, Finance can approve Net45 and quarterly+monthly invoicing. I can draft the invoicing annex language and attach to v3.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Ops (Finance), Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
